newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-JURY STILL CAN'T AGREE IN UK SOCCER FIXING TRIAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JURY STILL CAN'T AGREE IN UK SOCCER FIXING TRIAL.

text.p: The British jury in a sensational soccer match-fixing trial reported on Monday that it had still not been able to agree on its verdicts after two days of deliberation.

The judge at the court in Winchester, southern England, where the trial is now in its 43rd day, sent the five men and six women home for the night after their foreman reported their failure to come to any conclusions.

In the trial, former top players Bruce Grobbelaar, 39, John Fashanu, 34, Hans Segers, 35, and Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim, 32, are accused of conspiring to give or accept corrupt payments to influence the result of matches.
It is alleged they were part of a plot involving an Asian betting syndicate to rig English premier league games.
The four men deny the allegations.
Lim, former Aston Villa and Wimbledon striker Fashanu and former Wimbledon keeper Segers are accused of conspiring to rig matches between 1991 and 1994.
Separately, Lim, Fashanu and former Liverpool and Southampton goalkeeper Grobbelaar are accused of a similar conspiracy between November 1992 and November 1994.
Grobbelaar also denies accepting 2,000 pounds ($3,270) from his former business partner Christopher Vincent for fixing or trying to fix games.
The jury at a previous trial in the same case, which ended earlier this year, failed to reach a verdict. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
